text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Fatherland & Freedom says the call by President Guntis Ulmanis for parties to scrap the agre restrictions on people getting citizenship, mainly Russian-speakers, plays to the interests of Russian imperialists and is dangerous to Latvia's national statehood. The party warned that altering the law may lead to the government's collapse.

- EU Commissioner Hans van de Broek stressed that Latvia has to speed the law-making process in areas related to foreign trade, customs, competition and fight against money laundering. He pledged that Latvia will be given all the support it needs to further its integration with the EU.

- The ministers of defence of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia signed a joined statement in which they express readiness to implement three projects: Baltbat, Baltron and RASCC, which means the creation of a joint air space control system.

- Latvian and Lithuanian customs and border guard officials signed an agreement on the creation of a joint customs and border check point. The agreement will come into force on August 1 and is regarded as another step towards a closer integration of the three Baltic states.
- President Ulmanis is planning to visit France on April 13-16.
- On April 2, the budget surplus was 289,000 lats.
- Russian Ambassador Alexander Udaltsov believes the two countries should exchange trade representations to increase the trade volume.

- After signing the agreement on buying shares of Latvian Gas, Gazprom president Rem Vyakhirev is reported to have met the president of Parex Bank, Valery Kargin. No details have been disclosed. Earlier the bank made bids to buy Latvian Gas shares.
- Latvia started preparations for EXPO 2000 in Hannover, the international trade exhibition.
- The legal director of the Latvian Privatisation agency, Viktor Shadinov, has been recommended for a state medal.
